rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands, in manual and express mode
rows.failure_mode: Window reacts late to switch press (partial/late function)
rows.effect: Vehicle: delayed window start. Driver: window feels slow, complaint; not safety relevant.
rows.cause: Press/hold classification and debounce time in switch input is too long
rows.rating_reasons: S4: noticed by most customers as feel. O5: DR-1010 reports it without a measurement and no prevention exists. D7: no response-time test is targeted at it, review would not find a timing value.
rows.recommended_action: Measure switch-to-motor-command latency on the bench at 9, 13.5 and 16 V and add the limit to the SRS; adjust debounce if above it.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands, in manual and express mode
rows.failure_mode: Motor keeps running after switch release at high voltage (too late stop)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window overruns by 180 ms instead of max 100 ms. Driver/passenger: window travels further than intended, e.g. toward a hand or head at the edge, limit exceeded.
rows.cause: Motor-off command after release is not compensated for supply voltage (180 ms at 16 V vs 60 ms at 13.5 V)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: manual function degraded, anti-pinch still active. O8: DR-1014 shows the cause has occurred, no prevention. D6: found in a test, but no listed control targets release timing at 16 V.
rows.recommended_action: Find why release handling depends on voltage; fix the stop path and add a release-to-stop timing test at 9, 13.5 and 16 V to the HIL plan.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands, in manual and express mode
rows.failure_mode: Express close available when the window is not normalized (unintended function)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window closes fully in express mode with unknown position, so the pinch zone is not valid. Passenger: pinch could occur without protection; breaks a requirement.
rows.cause: Normalization state defaults to 'normalized' after battery disconnect (not cleared or not checked by the express request)
rows.rating_reasons: S9: possible injury and a requirement is broken. O9: DR-1020 shows it already happens. D5: a test found it, but no listed control targets power-loss states.
rows.recommended_action: Make normalization state default to 'not normalized' at cold start and gate express close and the anti-pinch zone on it; add a HIL test with battery disconnect at all positions.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands, in manual and express mode
rows.failure_mode: Window moves without a driver command (unintended function)
rows.effect: Vehicle: unexpected window movement. Passenger/child: can be trapped by a closing window with no warning.
rows.cause: Switch input misreads noise, a stuck contact or a short press as a held press
rows.rating_reasons: S10: injury with no warning. O3: no history, but no specific prevention either. D7: no test targets switch faults or EMC noise on the input.
rows.recommended_action: Add input plausibility (stuck switch, both directions pressed) and a HIL fault-injection test with noise and contact bounce on the switch lines.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands, in manual and express mode
rows.failure_mode: Retained power ends too early (window stops working about 45 s after ignition off instead of 60 s)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window cannot be operated within the specified time. Driver: window does not move after ignition off, can't close it when leaving.
rows.cause: Retained-power timer is wrong or restarts/ends early in the supply monitor
rows.rating_reasons: S6: comfort function lost after the shortened time. O9: DR-1002 and DR-1015 show it occurs. D4: a test found it, but only at some conditions.
rows.recommended_action: Correct the timer against SRS value (60 s) and add a timed retained-power test across voltage and temperature.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands, in manual and express mode
rows.failure_mode: Both H-bridge sides switched on, or motor moves in the wrong direction (unintended function)
rows.effect: Vehicle: driver stage short circuit, window does not move or moves wrongly. Driver: window opens when closing is commanded, or is lost.
rows.cause: Missing dead time or direction interlock in the H-bridge control
rows.rating_reasons: S8: main function lost. O3: no history, standard design. D7: no listed test targets the interlock.
rows.recommended_action: Verify dead time and interlock in design review and by scope measurement at 9 and 16 V and hot.

rows.function: 2. Stop the window at the end positions
rows.failure_mode: End stop not detected, motor keeps pushing
rows.effect: Vehicle: motor and regulator stressed until thermal protection acts. Driver: window pushes into the seal, noise.
rows.cause: End-stop current threshold is not reached (tolerance of current measurement, low voltage)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: main function degraded and hardware stress. O5: no history, no prevention, DR-1027 shows pushing after another cause. D6: no listed test targets end-stop detection.
rows.recommended_action: Add end-stop detection test across voltage and temperature, including worst-case current measurement tolerance.

rows.function: 2. Stop the window at the end positions
rows.failure_mode: Window hits the seal too hard (stop too late / at too high speed)
rows.effect: Vehicle: loud knock at the top end. Driver: noise noticed.
rows.cause: End-stop detected only by current rise, without speed reduction before the end position
rows.rating_reasons: S4: noise noticed by most customers. O7: DR-1026 reports it, from clinic drivers. D6: no listed test targets it, it was seen in a clinic.
rows.recommended_action: Add a soft-stop speed ramp near the end position, using the position counter once it is normalized; verify with a noise/speed measurement.

rows.function: 2. Stop the window at the end positions
rows.failure_mode: Motor stops before the end position in cold (early stop, partial function)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window not fully closed. Driver: gap at the top, wind noise or rain entering.
rows.cause: End-stop current threshold is crossed by high cold friction
rows.rating_reasons: S7: main function degraded. O5: cold stops seen in DR-1004 may be partly this, not confirmed. D6: no test targets end-stop at -30 °C.
rows.recommended_action: Include end-stop detection at -30 °C in the HIL tests; consider temperature-dependent threshold.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch in the pinch zone and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: Pinch stop too late when cold and at low supply (13 to 14 ms vs 10 ms)
rows.effect: Vehicle: pinch force exceeds the limit. Passenger: finger/hand or child's neck pinched with higher force; requirement broken.
rows.cause: Speed sampling and confirmation delay at low motor speed (cold grease, 9 V) are too long in the algorithm
prevention: Speed-ripple filter with 30 ms debounce (from LL-2021-07)
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S10: injury with no warning. O9: DR-1001 and DR-1006 are open and the same problem was in LL-2022-02. D3: TP-AP-01 covers the corner and found it.
rows.recommended_action: Reduce the confirmation time at low speed (check that the 2 ms sampling below 0 °C from LL-2022-02 is in WLC-200 software); re-run TP-AP-01 at -30 °C/9 V on every software release.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch in the pinch zone and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: Reversal distance too short when hot (146 mm vs 150 mm)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window does not open far enough after a pinch. Passenger: trapped part is not released, or stays loaded; requirement broken.
rows.cause: Reversal travel is not compensated for motor run-on and hot-temperature speed
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S9: possible injury with a requirement broken. O8: DR-1030 is open and no prevention exists. D3: TP-AP-01 covers 85 °C and found it.
rows.recommended_action: Define reversal as position-based with temperature margin; check the same at all voltages and at 23 °C (162 mm passed with little margin to a window of limits).

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch in the pinch zone and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: Pinch not detected at all
rows.effect: Vehicle: window closes fully on the object. Passenger: severe injury, especially a child.
rows.cause: Force threshold or force estimate error from current-measurement offset and tolerances is too large
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S10: injury with no warning. O4: algorithm proven in WLC-100 but motor and threshold are new, so open questions. D5: TP-AP-01 covers conditions but not hardware tolerance extremes or aged regulators.
rows.recommended_action: Add a tolerance study (current offset, gain, regulator friction, window seal stiffness) to TP-AP-01 with worst-case samples.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch in the pinch zone and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: False pinch reversal on rough road
rows.effect: Vehicle: window reverses by itself when closing. Driver: cannot close the window on cobblestones; cannot close when leaving.
rows.cause: Body vibration speed oscillation is read as rising pinch force in the algorithm
prevention: Speed-ripple filter with 30 ms debounce (from LL-2021-07)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: main function degraded on rough roads. O8: DR-1008 and DR-1023 are open though the filter exists. D4: the vibration profile targets it, but only some conditions (cobblestone at 30 km/h).
rows.recommended_action: Run the rough-road profile at the corners (cold, 9 V, 16 V, other speeds); check filter/debounce tuning against the 10 ms stop-time margin in LL-2021-07 after any change.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch in the pinch zone and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: False pinch reversal in cold without obstacle
rows.effect: Vehicle: window stops and reverses in express/auto close. Driver: window will not close in the morning; second try works.
rows.cause: Higher cold friction and speed ripple raise the force estimate; no temperature compensation of the threshold
prevention: Speed-ripple filter with 30 ms debounce (from LL-2021-07)
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: main function degraded. O8: DR-1004 and DR-1011 show it at -18 to -20 °C. D6: TP-AP-01 tests pinch detection, not false reversal without an obstacle in cold.
rows.recommended_action: Add cold no-obstacle closing runs (-30 to 0 °C, full cycle series) to the HIL tests; analyse force estimate against cold friction and adapt threshold.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch in the pinch zone and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: Anti-pinch fooled by start inrush (14 A at 16 V) at the start of closing
rows.effect: Vehicle: false reversal or masked pinch at the start of movement. Driver: window reverses at start, or pinch in the lower zone is missed.
rows.cause: Start-current transient is not blanked or modelled in the force estimate
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: false reversal degrades the main function. O4: inrush known from DR-1028 and the algorithm is similar to WLC-100, but no spec limit. D5: TP-AP-01 runs at 16 V but does not target the start.
rows.recommended_action: Define an inrush requirement and test closing starts at 16 V and at different window positions.

rows.function: 4. Keep track of window position
rows.failure_mode: Position drifts (3.5 mm error at the top seal after 200 cycles)
rows.effect: Vehicle: pinch zone and end stops are shifted. Passenger: pinch protection may be off at the edge of the zone; requirement affected.
rows.cause: Hall pulses are lost or double-counted at direction change and motor run-on after stop
prevention: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S9: possible injury through shifted pinch zone. O8: DR-1013 is open. D6: tests could find it, but none runs long cycle series with position check; the timeout does not detect drift.
rows.recommended_action: Count the run-on after stop and re-normalize at the top end stop; add an endurance test (>=1000 cycles) checking reported against real position.

rows.function: 4. Keep track of window position
rows.failure_mode: Hall signal lost: motor keeps running (1.2 s at 9 V, until the end stop)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window pushes into the seal; no position and no anti-pinch speed signal. Passenger: pinch possible without protection; motor overheats.
rows.cause: Plausibility timer restarts on noise at low speed, so the 200 ms timeout is not reached at 9 V
prevention: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
detection: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
rows.rating_reasons: S9: injury possible with the anti-pinch signal gone. O9: DR-1018 and DR-1027 are open; LL-2023-05 gave the same warning. D5: the Hall disconnect test exists in LL-2023-05 but is not in the structure's control list and found it at 9 V only.
rows.recommended_action: Make the timer immune to noise (restart only on valid pulse edges within a plausible period); add the Hall-disconnect HIL test at 9 V and 13.5 V, at several speeds, to the test plan.

rows.function: 4. Keep track of window position
rows.failure_mode: Hall signal intermittent (dropouts)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window stops or position is lost randomly. Driver: window stops mid-travel, must be re-normalized.
rows.cause: Corroded Hall connector pins give intermittent contact
detection: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
rows.rating_reasons: S7: main function degraded. O5: LL-2023-05 had 12 returns; the sealed connector is planned but not verified for WLC-200. D6: the timeout detects long loss, not short dropouts, and no corrosion test is listed.
rows.recommended_action: Confirm sealed connector in WLC-200; add a dropout-injection HIL test (1 to 150 ms gaps) and a salt-spray test of the connector.

rows.function: 5. Protect the motor from overheating
rows.failure_mode: Opening allowed once above the 140 °C limit (stale estimate)
rows.effect: Vehicle: motor gets one more movement while overheated, possible damage. Driver: window heats the motor further; no direct injury.
rows.cause: Block decision reads the thermal estimate before the thermal task has updated it (platform issue from LL-2024-01)
detection: Thermal model reviewed against thermocouple data (TP-TH-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: motor damage would degrade the main function. O9: DR-1012 and DR-1019 are open, and LL-2024-01 gave the warning. D4: TC-TH-03 found it, but TP-TH-01 only compares model and thermocouple, not timing.
rows.recommended_action: Check that the LL-2024-01 fix (decision read after the thermal task in the same cycle) is in the WLC-200 build; add a test that requests a movement right after the limit crossing.

rows.function: 5. Protect the motor from overheating
rows.failure_mode: Model underestimates motor temperature
rows.effect: Vehicle: motor overheats without limitation, damage. Driver: window fails later, no longer closes.
rows.cause: Thermal parameters (heat capacity, cooling) wrong for the WLC-200 motor or hot ambient
detection: Thermal model reviewed against thermocouple data (TP-TH-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S8: main function lost if the motor is damaged. O4: model proven in principle, new motor. D4: TP-TH-01 targets it but probably not all ambient and duty cycles.
rows.recommended_action: Extend TP-TH-01 to 85 °C ambient, locked rotor and repeated cycles; add margin on the limit.

rows.function: 5. Protect the motor from overheating
rows.failure_mode: Model overestimates temperature: unnecessary current limit or opening blocked
rows.effect: Vehicle: window slow or blocked while the motor is cool. Driver: window does not open or close fully in hot weather.
rows.cause: Conservative parameter or sensor offset in the current input of the thermal model
detection: Thermal model reviewed against thermocouple data (TP-TH-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S8: window can't close or open. O4: new motor, no history. D4: TP-TH-01 compares both directions of error but not all duty cycles.
rows.recommended_action: Include repeated normal use (e.g. 20 cycles in 85 °C) in TP-TH-01 to check for false blocks.

rows.function: 5. Protect the motor from overheating
rows.failure_mode: Thermal state lost after power loss (model restarts at ambient)
rows.effect: Vehicle: hot motor looks cold, protection late. Driver: no visible effect until motor damage.
rows.cause: Temperature estimate not kept through reset or battery disconnect
rows.rating_reasons: S7: motor damage possible. O5: no history, no prevention. D7: no test targets reset while hot.
rows.recommended_action: Define conservative start value after reset (e.g. last stored or elevated) and test a reset at 140 °C.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: WLC_Status frame missing (200 ms gap) during diagnostic requests
rows.effect: Vehicle: body controller logs a missing window controller and may not know the window state. Driver: probably none, maybe a wrong warning lamp.
rows.cause: A status frame is dropped when the transmit queue is busy with diagnostic responses, despite the sizing
prevention: CAN transmit queue sized for the worst-case bus load (from LL-2024-09)
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S5: status function degraded. O8: DR-1016 is open although the queue sizing exists. D4: TC-DG-03 found it once in 100 requests; a rare event may be missed.
rows.recommended_action: Check the dedicated status transmit buffer from LL-2024-09 exists in WLC-200; extend TC-DG-03 to thousands of requests with motor running.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: Overcurrent not reported: no DTC B1A02, fault state stays 0
rows.effect: Vehicle: motor stops but the fault is invisible to the body controller and service. Driver: window stops without explanation; service cannot find the cause.
rows.cause: Overcurrent diagnostic does not store the DTC or set the fault state after the motor stop
rows.rating_reasons: S5: diagnostic function degraded. O9: DR-1009 and DR-1029 are open. D4: TC-DG-02 targets it but it was only seen at the injected condition.
rows.recommended_action: Fix the DTC/fault state path; test overcurrent at different amplitudes, durations, voltages.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: No DTC B1A01 on Hall loss
rows.effect: Vehicle: Hall fault not stored. Driver: window problem remains undiagnosed in the workshop, repeat failures.
rows.cause: DTC is set only when the 200 ms timeout expires, which is never reached when the timer restarts (see Hall loss row)
prevention: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
detection: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
rows.rating_reasons: S5: diagnostic function lost. O9: DR-1018 and DR-1027 are open. D5: found by test, but the disconnect test is not in the listed controls. The link to the timer is a hypothesis for the team to confirm.
rows.recommended_action: Confirm the cause with the fix of the Hall timer; add a check of DTC B1A01 and fault state in the Hall disconnect HIL test.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: WLC_CloseAll executed unintentionally or without plausibility (unintended function)
rows.effect: Vehicle: windows close with no driver action. Passenger: can be trapped, especially a child, without warning.
rows.cause: Received CloseAll is not checked (no rolling counter, no check of vehicle state or normalization)
rows.rating_reasons: S9: possible injury, but anti-pinch stays active. O3: no history, but no check exists. D7: no listed test injects faulty CloseAll frames.
rows.recommended_action: Add message counter/plausibility check and a HIL test with corrupted, repeated and missing CloseAll frames; confirm CloseAll is blocked when not normalized.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: Diagnostic response too late (55 to 62 ms vs 50 ms)
rows.effect: Vehicle: diagnostic tester sees a timeout. Driver: none; workshop delay.
rows.cause: Diagnostic task is delayed by the motor start load in the scheduler
rows.rating_reasons: S3: noticed by some (workshop). O8: DR-1022 shows 3 in 100. D4: a test found it but only for some conditions.
rows.recommended_action: Analyse task priorities and worst-case timing during motor start; retest with more samples.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: Controller does not enter sleep (140 µA vs 100 µA)
rows.effect: Vehicle: battery drain when parked. Driver: flat battery after long standstill.
rows.cause: CAN transceiver stays in standby instead of sleep
rows.rating_reasons: S4: noticed by most customers after standstill. O9: DR-1007 is open. D4: a sleep current test targets it.
rows.recommended_action: Fix transceiver sleep command and wake-up logic; test sleep current with active and passive bus.

rows.function: 7. Behave safely at low and high supply voltage
rows.failure_mode: Undervoltage stop too late or controller reset while the motor runs
rows.effect: Vehicle: uncontrolled motor movement or loss of position during brownout. Driver: window may move without anti-pinch.
rows.cause: Undervoltage detection threshold or filter time in the supply monitor is too slow
rows.rating_reasons: S9: anti-pinch might be lost during movement. O3: 21 ms measured in DR-1025 within the 50 ms limit. D4: a test targets it at 5.5 V, maybe not all drops and slew rates.
rows.recommended_action: Test supply drops at different slew rates, start voltages and temperatures; check the margin to the 50 ms limit.

rows.function: 7. Behave safely at low and high supply voltage
rows.failure_mode: Manual-only mode entered on a short voltage dip (e.g. cranking)
rows.effect: Vehicle: express and anti-pinch switched off briefly. Driver: express mode not available after start.
rows.cause: Low-voltage threshold has no filter or hysteresis for short dips
rows.rating_reasons: S6: comfort function lost. O5: no history and no prevention. D6: tests could find it but none targets cranking profiles.
rows.recommended_action: Add cranking profile (ISO 16750-2) HIL tests with window operation.

rows.function: 7. Behave safely at low and high supply voltage
rows.failure_mode: Overvoltage (load dump) not handled: driver stage or controller damaged
rows.effect: Vehicle: controller fails after a load dump. Driver: window can't be moved.
rows.cause: Overvoltage protection and high-voltage threshold are not designed for load dump
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S8: main function lost. O4: standard design but new. D7: TP-AP-01 goes only to 16 V and does not target load dump.
rows.recommended_action: Add load-dump test (ISO 16750-2) and check voltage behaviour above 16 V in the design.

rows.function: 7. Behave safely at low and high supply voltage
rows.failure_mode: Reverse polarity kills the controller (protection diode D3 open)
rows.effect: Vehicle: controller dead after a reverse-battery event. Driver: window can't be moved, no fault shown.
rows.cause: Reverse-polarity protection diode D3 is under-rated for -14 V for 60 s
rows.rating_reasons: S8: main function lost. O8: DR-1024 shows it occurs. D4: the test found it, but only at one condition.
rows.recommended_action: Re-size D3 (or use a protection MOSFET) and repeat the reverse-polarity test with several samples and temperatures.

rows.cause: Received CloseAll is not checked (no rolling counter, no check of vehicle state or normalization)
rows.rating_reasons: S9: possible injury, but anti-pinch stays active. O3: no history, but no check exists. D7: no listed test injects faulty CloseAll frames.
rows.recommended_action: Add message counter/plausibility check and a HIL test with corrupted, repeated and missing CloseAll frames; confirm CloseAll is blocked when not normalized.

rows.function: 7. Behave safely at low and high supply voltage
rows.failure_mode: Undervoltage stop too late or controller reset while the motor runs
rows.effect: Vehicle: uncontrolled motor movement or loss of position during brownout. Driver: window may move without anti-pinch.
rows.cause: Undervoltage detection threshold or filter time in the supply monitor is too slow
rows.rating_reasons: S9: anti-pinch might be lost during movement. O3: 21 ms measured in DR-1025 within the 50 ms limit. D4: a test targets it at 5.5 V, maybe not all drops and slew rates.
rows.recommended_action: Test supply drops at different slew rates, start voltages and temperatures; check the margin to the 50 ms limit.

rows.function: 7. Behave safely at low and high supply voltage
rows.failure_mode: Reverse polarity kills the controller (protection diode D3 open)
rows.effect: Vehicle: controller dead after a reverse-battery event. Driver: window can't be moved, no fault shown.
rows.cause: Reverse-polarity protection diode D3 is under-rated for -14 V for 60 s
rows.rating_reasons: S8: main function lost. O8: DR-1024 shows it occurs. D4: the test found it, but only at one condition.
rows.recommended_action: Re-size D3 (or use a protection MOSFET) and repeat the reverse-polarity test with several samples and temperatures.

rows.function: 7. Behave safely at low and high supply voltage
rows.failure_mode: Overvoltage (load dump) not handled: driver stage or controller damaged
rows.effect: Vehicle: controller fails after a load dump. Driver: window can't be moved.
rows.cause: Overvoltage protection and high-voltage threshold are not designed for load dump
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S8: main function lost. O4: standard design but new. D7: TP-AP-01 goes only to 16 V and does not target load dump.
rows.recommended_action: Add load-dump test (ISO 16750-2) and check voltage behaviour above 16 V in the design.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands, in manual and express mode
rows.failure_mode: Both H-bridge sides switched on, or motor moves in the wrong direction (unintended function)
rows.effect: Vehicle: driver stage short circuit, window does not move or moves wrongly. Driver: window opens when closing is commanded, or is lost.
rows.cause: Missing dead time or direction interlock in the H-bridge control
rows.rating_reasons: S8: main function lost. O3: no history, standard design. D7: no listed test targets the interlock.
rows.recommended_action: Verify dead time and interlock in design review and by scope measurement at 9 and 16 V and hot.

rows.function: 5. Protect the motor from overheating
rows.failure_mode: Model underestimates motor temperature
rows.effect: Vehicle: motor overheats without limitation, damage. Driver: window fails later, no longer closes.
rows.cause: Thermal parameters (heat capacity, cooling) wrong for the WLC-200 motor or hot ambient
detection: Thermal model reviewed against thermocouple data (TP-TH-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S8: main function lost if the motor is damaged. O4: model proven in principle, new motor. D4: TP-TH-01 targets it but probably not all ambient and duty cycles.
rows.recommended_action: Extend TP-TH-01 to 85 °C ambient, locked rotor and repeated cycles; add margin on the limit.

rows.function: 5. Protect the motor from overheating
rows.failure_mode: Model overestimates temperature: unnecessary current limit or opening blocked
rows.effect: Vehicle: window slow or blocked while the motor is cool. Driver: window does not open or close fully in hot weather.
rows.cause: Conservative parameter or sensor offset in the current input of the thermal model
detection: Thermal model reviewed against thermocouple data (TP-TH-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S8: window can't close or open. O4: new motor, no history. D4: TP-TH-01 compares both directions of error but not all duty cycles.
rows.recommended_action: Include repeated normal use (e.g. 20 cycles in 85 °C) in TP-TH-01 to check for false blocks.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands, in manual and express mode
rows.failure_mode: Motor keeps running after switch release at high voltage (too late stop)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window overruns by 180 ms instead of max 100 ms. Driver/passenger: window travels further than intended, e.g. toward a hand or head at the edge, limit exceeded.
rows.cause: Motor-off command after release is not compensated for supply voltage (180 ms at 16 V vs 60 ms at 13.5 V)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: manual function degraded, anti-pinch still active. O8: DR-1014 shows the cause has occurred, no prevention. D6: found in a test, but no listed control targets release timing at 16 V.
rows.recommended_action: Find why release handling depends on voltage; fix the stop path and add a release-to-stop timing test at 9, 13.5 and 16 V to the HIL plan.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch in the pinch zone and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: False pinch reversal in cold without obstacle
rows.effect: Vehicle: window stops and reverses in express/auto close. Driver: window will not close in the morning; second try works.
rows.cause: Higher cold friction and speed ripple raise the force estimate; no temperature compensation of the threshold
prevention: Speed-ripple filter with 30 ms debounce (from LL-2021-07)
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: main function degraded. O8: DR-1004 and DR-1011 show it at -18 to -20 °C. D6: TP-AP-01 tests pinch detection, not false reversal without an obstacle in cold.
rows.recommended_action: Add cold no-obstacle closing runs (-30 to 0 °C, full cycle series) to the HIL tests; analyse force estimate against cold friction and adapt threshold.

rows.function: 5. Protect the motor from overheating
rows.failure_mode: Opening allowed once above the 140 °C limit (stale estimate)
rows.effect: Vehicle: motor gets one more movement while overheated, possible damage. Driver: window heats the motor further; no direct injury.
rows.cause: Block decision reads the thermal estimate before the thermal task has updated it (platform issue from LL-2024-01)
detection: Thermal model reviewed against thermocouple data (TP-TH-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: motor damage would degrade the main function. O9: DR-1012 and DR-1019 are open, and LL-2024-01 gave the warning. D4: TC-TH-03 found it, but TP-TH-01 only compares model and thermocouple, not timing.
rows.recommended_action: Check that the LL-2024-01 fix (decision read after the thermal task in the same cycle) is in the WLC-200 build; add a test that requests a movement right after the limit crossing.

rows.function: 5. Protect the motor from overheating
rows.failure_mode: Thermal state lost after power loss (model restarts at ambient)
rows.effect: Vehicle: hot motor looks cold, protection late. Driver: no visible effect until motor damage.
rows.cause: Temperature estimate not kept through reset or battery disconnect
rows.rating_reasons: S7: motor damage possible. O5: no history, no prevention. D7: no test targets reset while hot.
rows.recommended_action: Define conservative start value after reset (e.g. last stored or elevated) and test a reset at 140 °C.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch in the pinch zone and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: False pinch reversal on rough road
rows.effect: Vehicle: window reverses by itself when closing. Driver: cannot close the window on cobblestones; cannot close when leaving.
rows.cause: Body vibration speed oscillation is read as rising pinch force in the algorithm
prevention: Speed-ripple filter with 30 ms debounce (from LL-2021-07)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: main function degraded on rough roads. O8: DR-1008 and DR-1023 are open though the filter exists. D4: the vibration profile targets it, but only some conditions (cobblestone at 30 km/h).
rows.recommended_action: Run the rough-road profile at the corners (cold, 9 V, 16 V, other speeds); check filter/debounce tuning against the 10 ms stop-time margin in LL-2021-07 after any change.

rows.function: 2. Stop the window at the end positions
rows.failure_mode: End stop not detected, motor keeps pushing
rows.effect: Vehicle: motor and regulator stressed until thermal protection acts. Driver: window pushes into the seal, noise.
rows.cause: End-stop current threshold is not reached (tolerance of current measurement, low voltage)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: main function degraded and hardware stress. O5: no history, no prevention, DR-1027 shows pushing after another cause. D6: no listed test targets end-stop detection.
rows.recommended_action: Add end-stop detection test across voltage and temperature, including worst-case current measurement tolerance.

rows.function: 2. Stop the window at the end positions
rows.failure_mode: Motor stops before the end position in cold (early stop, partial function)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window not fully closed. Driver: gap at the top, wind noise or rain entering.
rows.cause: End-stop current threshold is crossed by high cold friction
rows.rating_reasons: S7: main function degraded. O5: cold stops seen in DR-1004 may be partly this, not confirmed. D6: no test targets end-stop at -30 °C.
rows.recommended_action: Include end-stop detection at -30 °C in the HIL tests; consider temperature-dependent threshold.

rows.function: 4. Keep track of window position
rows.failure_mode: Hall signal intermittent (dropouts)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window stops or position is lost randomly. Driver: window stops mid-travel, must be re-normalized.
rows.cause: Corroded Hall connector pins give intermittent contact
detection: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
rows.rating_reasons: S7: main function degraded. O5: LL-2023-05 had 12 returns; the sealed connector is planned but not verified for WLC-200. D6: the timeout detects long loss, not short dropouts, and no corrosion test is listed.
rows.recommended_action: Confirm sealed connector in WLC-200; add a dropout-injection HIL test (1 to 150 ms gaps) and a salt-spray test of the connector.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch in the pinch zone and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: Anti-pinch fooled by start inrush (14 A at 16 V) at the start of closing
rows.effect: Vehicle: false reversal or masked pinch at the start of movement. Driver: window reverses at start, or pinch in the lower zone is missed.
rows.cause: Start-current transient is not blanked or modelled in the force estimate
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: false reversal degrades the main function. O4: inrush known from DR-1028 and the algorithm is similar to WLC-100, but no spec limit. D5: TP-AP-01 runs at 16 V but does not target the start.
rows.recommended_action: Define an inrush requirement and test closing starts at 16 V and at different window positions.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands, in manual and express mode
rows.failure_mode: Retained power ends too early (window stops working about 45 s after ignition off instead of 60 s)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window cannot be operated within the specified time. Driver: window does not move after ignition off, can't close it when leaving.
rows.cause: Retained-power timer is wrong or restarts/ends early in the supply monitor
rows.rating_reasons: S6: comfort function lost after the shortened time. O9: DR-1002 and DR-1015 show it occurs. D4: a test found it, but only at some conditions.
rows.recommended_action: Correct the timer against SRS value (60 s) and add a timed retained-power test across voltage and temperature.

rows.function: 7. Behave safely at low and high supply voltage
rows.failure_mode: Manual-only mode entered on a short voltage dip (e.g. cranking)
rows.effect: Vehicle: express and anti-pinch switched off briefly. Driver: express mode not available after start.
rows.cause: Low-voltage threshold has no filter or hysteresis for short dips
rows.rating_reasons: S6: comfort function lost. O5: no history and no prevention. D6: tests could find it but none targets cranking profiles.
rows.recommended_action: Add cranking profile (ISO 16750-2) HIL tests with window operation.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: No DTC B1A01 on Hall loss
rows.effect: Vehicle: Hall fault not stored. Driver: window problem remains undiagnosed in the workshop, repeat failures.
rows.cause: DTC is set only when the 200 ms timeout expires, which is never reached when the timer restarts (see Hall loss row)
prevention: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
detection: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
rows.rating_reasons: S5: diagnostic function lost. O9: DR-1018 and DR-1027 are open. D5: found by test, but the disconnect test is not in the listed controls. The link to the timer is a hypothesis for the team to confirm.
rows.recommended_action: Confirm the cause with the fix of the Hall timer; add a check of DTC B1A01 and fault state in the Hall disconnect HIL test.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: Overcurrent not reported: no DTC B1A02, fault state stays 0
rows.effect: Vehicle: motor stops but the fault is invisible to the body controller and service. Driver: window stops without explanation; service cannot find the cause.
rows.cause: Overcurrent diagnostic does not store the DTC or set the fault state after the motor stop
rows.rating_reasons: S5: diagnostic function degraded. O9: DR-1009 and DR-1029 are open. D4: TC-DG-02 targets it but it was only seen at the injected condition.
rows.recommended_action: Fix the DTC/fault state path; test overcurrent at different amplitudes, durations, voltages.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: WLC_Status frame missing (200 ms gap) during diagnostic requests
rows.effect: Vehicle: body controller logs a missing window controller and may not know the window state. Driver: probably none, maybe a wrong warning lamp.
rows.cause: A status frame is dropped when the transmit queue is busy with diagnostic responses, despite the sizing
prevention: CAN transmit queue sized for the worst-case bus load (from LL-2024-09)
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S5: status function degraded. O8: DR-1016 is open although the queue sizing exists. D4: TC-DG-03 found it once in 100 requests; a rare event may be missed.
rows.recommended_action: Check the dedicated status transmit buffer from LL-2024-09 exists in WLC-200; extend TC-DG-03 to thousands of requests with motor running.

rows.function: 2. Stop the window at the end positions
rows.failure_mode: Window hits the seal too hard (stop too late / at too high speed)
rows.effect: Vehicle: loud knock at the top end. Driver: noise noticed.
rows.cause: End-stop detected only by current rise, without speed reduction before the end position
rows.rating_reasons: S4: noise noticed by most customers. O7: DR-1026 reports it, from clinic drivers. D6: no listed test targets it, it was seen in a clinic.
rows.recommended_action: Add a soft-stop speed ramp near the end position, using the position counter once it is normalized; verify with a noise/speed measurement.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: Controller does not enter sleep (140 µA vs 100 µA)
rows.effect: Vehicle: battery drain when parked. Driver: flat battery after long standstill.
rows.cause: CAN transceiver stays in standby instead of sleep
rows.rating_reasons: S4: noticed by most customers after standstill. O9: DR-1007 is open. D4: a sleep current test targets it.
rows.recommended_action: Fix transceiver sleep command and wake-up logic; test sleep current with active and passive bus.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands, in manual and express mode
rows.failure_mode: Window reacts late to switch press (partial/late function)
rows.effect: Vehicle: delayed window start. Driver: window feels slow, complaint; not safety relevant.
rows.cause: Press/hold classification and debounce time in switch input is too long
rows.rating_reasons: S4: noticed by most customers as feel. O5: DR-1010 reports it without a measurement and no prevention exists. D7: no response-time test is targeted at it, review would not find a timing value.
rows.recommended_action: Measure switch-to-motor-command latency on the bench at 9, 13.5 and 16 V and add the limit to the SRS; adjust debounce if above it.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: Diagnostic response too late (55 to 62 ms vs 50 ms)
rows.effect: Vehicle: diagnostic tester sees a timeout. Driver: none; workshop delay.
rows.cause: Diagnostic task is delayed by the motor start load in the scheduler
rows.rating_reasons: S3: noticed by some (workshop). O8: DR-1022 shows 3 in 100. D4: a test found it but only for some conditions.
rows.recommended_action: Analyse task priorities and worst-case timing during motor start; retest with more samples.
